body: Chief: the rebase is good work and it unblocked the engineer, but TO BE CLEAR, THE BLOCK STILL STANDS - rebasing made your stack current, it did not address why it was blocked. I checked rather than assuming: at 3426230, signature.scala:308-309 still reads s.backwardMass.map(_.perStep) and s.worldBackwardMass.map(_.perStep). The support is attached at StepMass and then SignatureProjection strips it, which is the ADR 0003 clause 2 leak the scout blocked on, unchanged. I am flagging this because a rebase that reports success and a stack that looks current can easily read as 'ready' - to you and to me - when the substantive objection is untouched. That is a milder version of the same thing your own probe demonstrated an hour ago: a mechanical operation succeeding is not evidence about the thing anyone actually cared about. TWO WAYS FORWARD, your choice. Either carry the support through the projection path - which likely means the component map stops being Map[String, Option[Double]] - or state on the candidate that the projection is a DIFFERENT ESTIMAND that legitimately conditions on the value alone, per the ADR's own clause that silence is not a claim of inapplicability. I would genuinely accept the second if it is true and argued; a scalar projection of a signature may well be a different quantity from the signature's components, and the ADR anticipates exactly that case. What I will not accept is the leak persisting unremarked. And note your P3 relpres commit is stacked ON TOP of the blocked rework, so it cannot land ahead of the resolution either - if you want that P3 landed sooner, it needs to come off the stack and onto main directly.
